picks.title: Natsume Yuujinchou
picks.case: This is the answer to your prompt without qualification: episodic, gentle, one supernatural encounter per episode resolved by understanding rather than force. Where Mushishi keeps Ginko at arm's length from the people he helps, Natsume gives its lead friends and lets that hurt, so it is warmer than the thing you asked for and no less quiet. Given that you scored Mushishi a 10 and are currently working through Yuru Camp, the pace should be exactly right.

picks.title: Kino no Tabi
picks.case: Structurally this is the closest thing in the pool to Mushishi, a traveller who arrives, observes a self-contained strangeness and declines to interfere. It is colder than Aria the Animation and much less consoling, but it has the same refusal to hurry. Thirteen episodes, each of them self-contained.

picks.title: Ginga Tetsudou no Yoru
picks.case: A single film rather than a series, and the most purely atmospheric thing here. It shares Mushishi's willingness to let a sequence run long because the mood is the point, and it shares Aria the Animation's belief that a journey can be its own subject. It is the shortest commitment in this list and the one most likely to stay with you.
